strengths: The paper addresses an important phenomenon: adversarial training can preserve clean generalization while exhibiting a large robust generalization gap. The CGRO definition makes the target behavior explicit.
The decomposition into true-feature learning and sample-specific noise memorization provides an interpretable mechanistic hypothesis and concrete quantities to investigate.

The reported CIFAR10 results clearly illustrate the motivating phenomenon. Capacity sweeps, synthetic feature trajectories, and supplementary flatness measurements provide useful qualitative observations.
weaknesses: Theorem 4.4 is false under its stated assumptions. Consider the uniform distribution on ±e1 with labels ±1, δ=1/4, and f_clean(x)=x1−0.9. This satisfies Assumptions 4.1–4.3. With polynomially many samples, both atoms have nonvanishing empirical frequencies with high probability, so vanishing robust training error forces zero robust test error; a CGRO classifier cannot exist. The proof also incorrectly infers disjoint same-class training balls from inter-class separation. Appendix F additionally claims uniform o(1) approximation of a discontinuous indicator-based function by continuous ReLU networks. These issues require stronger distributional assumptions and a revised construction.

Theorem 5.9 is incompatible with the full l2 robustness definition in Section 3. Training attacks modify only the signal direction. Under the claimed feature regime, replacing every noise patch by −c times itself makes α^q U−c^q V_i negative for a sufficiently large constant c. The perturbation costs O(σ_p√(dP))=o(δ) under Assumption 5.7. Thus the claimed positive noise memorization actually permits valid full-ball attacks on training examples, contradicting the asserted small robust training error. The theorem needs a consistently restricted threat model or a substantively different guarantee.

The test-error proof in Theorem E.12 contains further substantive gaps. It treats sums of cubic Gaussian projections as sub-Gaussian, although these generally have heavier tails and the terms sharing a noise patch are correlated. It also infers that every orthogonal weight component has norm Θ(1) from aggregate memorization V_i=Θ(1), which does not follow. The generalization conclusions therefore remain unsupported even after restricting the threat model.

The supplementary flatness bound in Theorem B.1 also fails as stated. A nonzero constant classifier has zero input-gradient flatness, yet random class frequencies can make its empirical logistic risk smaller than its population risk with probability approaching one half. The stated high-probability bound allows no such gap. Appendix G also leaves unexplained how its additive density-estimation terms and fixed perturbation radius produce the claimed sample-size rate.

The synthetic experiment uses δ=α=10, violating the theorem's requirement δ<α and allowing complete erasure of the meaningful signal. Consequently, it does not validate the proposed mechanism in the stated theoretical regime. The real-image capacity and flatness measurements do not isolate noise memorization as the cause of the gap. Missing PGD step counts, step sizes, restart settings, complete training specifications, and variability across seeds further limit reproducibility and confidence in robustness estimates.

The originality of Theorem 4.7 needs clearer justification relative to Li et al. (2022). Appendix F still constructs a linearly separable hard distribution; enlarging the admissible distribution class to those with polynomial-size clean classifiers does not strengthen that existential result. The dynamics analysis is the most promising additional contribution, but the central correctness issues above prevent it from supporting acceptance.
